# Dataset card — ShipIntel synthetic shipping documents

**Synthetic data only.** Every document and label was generated by `scripts/generate_synthetic_data.py`
(seed 42, deterministic: `python scripts/generate_synthetic_data.py`). Vessel and company names are random word
combinations and may coincide with real ones by accident; no real shipping record, company document or personal data
was used or imitated. Each document carries a visible `[SYNTHETIC SAMPLE …]` footer and each annotation has `"synthetic": true`.

## Composition

| | Dev | Held-out test |
|---|---|---|
| Templates | D1 bill of lading · D2 fixture recap · D3 cargo manifest · D4 notice of readiness · D5 shipping instruction · D6 voyage summary | T1 charter-party summary (numbered clauses) · T2 consignment advice · T3 voyage e-mail |
| Documents | 96 | 54 |
| Normal / injected-problem / non-shipping | 51 / 42 / 3 | 30 / 21 / 3 |
| Formats | TXT and PDF (≈35% PDF, generated with reportlab; table and plain-line layouts) | same |

Files: `data/samples/SI-NNNN.{txt,pdf}` · Labels: `data/annotations/{dev,test}.jsonl` with
`document_id, file, split, template, synthetic, kind, expected{10 fields}, expected_warnings[]`.

**Split policy:** by *template*, so layouts in the test split are unseen by the rules. Test templates were also given
different label wording. See the evaluation report for what this does and does not guarantee.

## Variation injected

Label typos (4% per label) · port spelling noise (known ports) · ports as `Name`, `NAME`, `Name, Country`, `Name (LOCODE)` ·
7 date formats · plain, comma, space and European-decimal numbers · 2–5 spellings per unit · ports outside the
built-in gazetteer (~10%) · distractor dates, numbers and parties · per-field omissions · wrapped prose.
Injected problems: ambiguous date, invalid date, discharge-before-loading, same origin/destination, zero quantity, non-shipping text.

## Annotation guidelines (ground-truth conventions)

| Field | Convention |
|---|---|
| `vessel_name` | Upper-case, without prefix (`M/V`, `MV`), voyage suffix or IMO. |
| `origin_port` / `destination_port` | Port name without country, code or "Port of"; canonical spelling of the intended port even if the document is misspelled. |
| `cargo_type` | Canonical title case (acronyms kept, e.g. `LNG`); tolerance, "approx." and "in bulk" removed; `Liquefied Natural Gas` → `LNG`. |
| `cargo_quantity` / `cargo_unit` | Number as a float; unit canonical `MT, kg, bbl, TEU, m3`. Zero quantity → quantity `null` (unit kept), warning `NONPOSITIVE_QUANTITY`. |
| `loading_date` / `discharge_date` | ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` of the date labelled loading/shipped-on-board and discharge/delivery. Issue/invoice/advice dates are distractors. ETA is not used. **Ambiguous numeric dates (`03/04/2025`) and impossible dates → `null`** with `AMBIGUOUS_DATE` / `INVALID_DATE`. Discharge before loading: both dates kept, warning `DISCHARGE_BEFORE_LOADING`. |
| `document_reference` | Identifier as written (B/L, fixture, CP, manifest, document or shipment reference). Invoice, voyage and IMO numbers are distractors. |
| `counterparty` | Priority **charterer > shipper > consignee > buyer** among roles present in the document; company name without address. Owner/carrier and notify party are not counterparties. |
| Missing | A field omitted from the document is `null`. |

## Intended use and limits

For developing and demonstrating the pipeline, and for testing the evaluation code. **Not** suitable for estimating real-world
accuracy; the generator and the extraction rules share an author, port names overlap with the gazetteer, and layouts are far simpler than
real documents. Free to reuse (MIT).
